newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firm on dollar flow to bourse.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firm on dollar flow to bourse.

text.p: The Mexican peso opened firmer across the board on moderate capital inflow to the local bourse, dealers said.

"Some foreign players are switching from dollars to enter the bourse, and that could offset pressure from exercising dollar put options," a dealer said, referring to $500 million in puts auctioned by the central bank on July 31.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were 1.0 and 0.85 of a centavo firmer in the early minutes of trade at 7.8030/7.8050 and 7.8015/7.8035 per dollar, respectively.
Same-day peso contracts were meanwhile 2.5 centavos firmer at 7.7970/7.8000 per dollar.
The Mexican bourse's IPC index was meanwhile up 0.59 percent to 5,165.33 points.

Dealers estimated that banks could choose to exercise put options if the peso continued to trade at less than 7.8100 per dollar, which would prevent the peso from becoming stronger. ((-Alexis Quiones, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9555))
